name: Fix a Service with no endpoints
objective: CKAD › Services & Networking. questions.title: Diagnose & fix: a Service with no endpoints
questions.teach:
A Service with **no endpoints** but healthy pods almost always means a **selector mismatch**. Compare the Service's `spec.selector` to the actual pod labels, then patch it in place.

**Gotcha:** fix the selector; don't delete and recreate the Service.
questions.prompt:
Service `api-svc` in `svcnet-learn` has **no endpoints** even though Deployment `api` (label `app=api`) is running. Diagnose and fix it so the Service has endpoints. Don't delete it.

Target: `api-svc` has at least one endpoint address.
questions.hint: `kubectl -n svcnet-learn get endpoints api-svc` (empty) then `kubectl -n svcnet-learn get svc api-svc -o jsonpath='{.spec.selector}'` — the selector is wrong. Patch it to `app=api`: `kubectl -n svcnet-learn patch svc api-svc -p '{"spec":{"selector":{"app":"api"}}}'`.
questions.solution:
kubectl -n svcnet-learn patch svc api-svc -p '{"spec":{"selector":{"app":"api"}}}'
kubectl -n svcnet-learn get endpoints api-svc

verification.description: api-svc now has endpoints (selector fixed to app=api)

questions.eli5:
A Service finds its pods by matching **labels** — it carries a little "I'm looking for people wearing *this* badge" note called a `selector`. The pods wear badges (labels). When the note matches the badges, Kubernetes builds a list of those pods (the **endpoints**) and the Service forwards traffic to them.

Service `api-svc` has **no endpoints** — an empty forwarding list — even though the `api` Deployment is up and healthy. The pods are fine; the Service's note just has the **wrong badge on it**. It's looking for, say, `app=apiserver` while the pods actually wear `app=api`. No match, no endpoints, no traffic.

The fix is to correct the Service's selector so it matches the real pod labels, then the endpoints populate on their own.

Diagnosis flow:
- `kubectl get endpoints api-svc` → empty confirms the problem.
- `kubectl get svc api-svc -o jsonpath='{.spec.selector}'` → see what it's looking for.
- Compare to `kubectl get pods --show-labels` → see what the pods actually wear.
- Patch the selector to match: `kubectl patch svc api-svc -p '{"spec":{"selector":{"app":"api"}}}'`.

**Watch out for:**

- **Fix the selector, don't delete the Service.** The task forbids recreating it — patch it in place.
- Confirm the pods' **actual** labels before patching; guessing a label that doesn't exist just leaves it broken differently.
- Empty endpoints almost always means a **selector/label mismatch** — but double-check the pods are really Ready (a not-Ready pod is also kept out of endpoints).
- After patching, re-check `get endpoints` to confirm addresses appeared; the selector match is instant but verify it.
questions.deepDive:
## Diagnose & fix: a Service with no endpoints

### Mental model
A Service with a selector auto-populates its **EndpointSlices/Endpoints** from pods whose labels match `spec.selector` **and** that are **Ready**. "Healthy pods but empty endpoints" almost always means the **selector doesn't match the pod labels**. Fix the selector in place.

### Diagnosis chain
```bash
kubectl -n svcnet-learn get endpoints api-svc                 # empty / <none>
kubectl -n svcnet-learn get svc api-svc -o jsonpath='{.spec.selector}{"\n"}'   # what it looks for
kubectl -n svcnet-learn get pods -l app=api --show-labels     # what pods actually wear
kubectl -n svcnet-learn get pods --show-labels                # full label picture
```
If the Service selector (e.g. `{app: apiserver}`) differs from the pod labels (`{app: api}`), that's the bug.

### The fix — patch the selector
```bash
kubectl -n svcnet-learn patch svc api-svc -p '{"spec":{"selector":{"app":"api"}}}'
kubectl -n svcnet-learn get endpoints api-svc                 # now shows pod IPs
```
Or `kubectl -n svcnet-learn edit svc api-svc` and correct `spec.selector`.

### Why endpoints can be empty — full checklist
| Cause | Check |
|---|---|
| **Selector/label mismatch** (most common) | compare `svc .spec.selector` vs pod labels |
| Pods not **Ready** | `kubectl get pods` READY column; failing readiness probe excludes a pod |
| Wrong namespace | Service and pods must share a namespace |
| `targetPort`/port name mismatch | named targetPort not present on pod |
| Selector-less Service by design | no selector → needs manual EndpointSlice |

> A **not-Ready** pod is intentionally kept out of endpoints — verify readiness, not just "Running".

### Verify the match logic
Selector is an **AND** of exact key=value pairs; a pod must carry *all* of them (and may carry extras). `app: api` matches a pod labelled `app=api,track=stable`; it does **not** match `app=apiserver`.

### Gotchas & exam traps
- **Patch/edit the selector — don't delete and recreate** the Service.
- Verify the **real** pod labels first (`--show-labels`); don't patch to a guessed value.
- Empty endpoints ≠ always selector: also rule out **readiness** and **namespace**.
- `kubectl get endpoints` and `get endpointslices` give the same answer two ways.
- After patching, endpoint population is immediate — re-check to confirm.

### Quick reference
```bash
kubectl -n svcnet-learn get endpoints api-svc                      # empty
kubectl -n svcnet-learn get svc api-svc -o jsonpath='{.spec.selector}'
kubectl -n svcnet-learn get pods --show-labels                     # find real labels
kubectl -n svcnet-learn patch svc api-svc -p '{"spec":{"selector":{"app":"api"}}}'
kubectl -n svcnet-learn get endpoints api-svc                      # now populated
```
